name: India Geodata — unified Indian geospatial data repository
publisher: yashveeeeeeer (community aggregation of Government of India sources)
caveats: third-party mirror, not an authority
per-dataset licences vary; some CC0 claims sit over upstream material with unstated terms
vintages differ by layer and are often undocumented
large files are GitHub Release assets, not repo files
evidence: Read top-level README plus 10 sub-dataset READMEs and data/police/metadata.json via raw.githubusercontent.com. Catalogue spans ~1,800 files in 14 collections: administrative ~27GB, water ~18.5GB, infrastructure ~20GB, postal ~700MB, urban ~430MB, police ~101MB. Downloaded and fully parsed one dataset (16,459 features).
notes: Fastest single route to nearly every boundary layer this product needs. PMTiles output means boundary tiles can be served from object storage with no tile server.

name: Police station (thana) jurisdiction boundaries — 7 states + marine
publisher: State GIS agencies: APSAC, i-Bhugoal, GSDL, KGIS, Rajdharaa, TNGIS, TRACGIS, NCOG
geo_coverage: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Delhi, Karnataka, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Telangana + Indian marine zones
license: CC0-1.0 as asserted by the mirror; upstream state-portal terms unstated
caveats: ONLY 7 of 36 states/UTs — no thana polygon exists publicly for the other 29
vintage per state undocumented
traffic/railway/GRP jurisdictions OVERLAP territorial ones, so point-in-polygon returns a SET not a value
CC0 is the mirror's assertion, not the states'
no published crosswalk to MHA ps_cd; names must be fuzzy-matched
boundaries change on thana bifurcation with no changelog
evidence: Release page lists 13 assets with per-state attribution: NCOG_Marine_Police_Boundaries, APSAC_Police_station_boundaries, Bhugoal_BH_Police_Thana_Boundaries, GSDL_DL_Police_Station_Boundaries, KGISMAPS_KN_Police/Railway/Traffic_Station_Boundaries, Rajdharaa_RJ_Police_Thana_Boundary + _GRP_, TNGIS_TN_Police + _Traffic_Station_Boundaries, TRACGIS_TG_Police_Station_Boundaries. india-geodata data/police/README.md independently tabulates the same 8 sources: '~36 files, ~96 MB'. Archives not decompressed.
notes: THE answer to the central question: India's equivalent of police.uk neighbourhood boundaries exists, but only for ~1/3 of the population.

name: All-India police station point locations (MHA station master)
publisher: Ministry of Home Affairs (NIC-served GeoServer layer; mirrored on GitHub)
caveats: state_cd is the MHA/NCRB alphabetical series (1=A&N, 2=AP, 29=TN, 37=TG), NOT Census 2011 codes (AP=28, TN=33) — crosswalk mandatory
codes 9 and 36 absent from the series
843 of 16,459 stations carry a ps_cd whose embedded district code contradicts their current district_c — stale post-reorganisation codes
only 14,647 distinct names for 16,459 stations: names are NOT unique even within a state, never join on name alone
Assam 324 and West Bengal 452 look low vs published force strength — coverage likely incomplete in some states
no timestamp/validity field
coordinates locate the station building, not a jurisdiction centroid
evidence: Downloaded 5,269,146 bytes and parsed in full: 16,459 Point features, schema [state,state_cd,district,district_c,ps,ps_cd,latitude,longitude] all 100% non-null; 36 distinct state_cd, 983 distinct district_c, 964 distinct district names, 16,459 unique ps_cd; bbox lat 7.01653-34.84755, lon 68.53847-97.006616; 0 zero-coords, 0 out-of-bbox. Feature ids are 'police_station_mha.N'. Code hierarchy district_c=state_cd*1000+d and ps_cd=district_c*1000+p holds for 15,616/16,459 (94.9%).
notes: Highest-value single file found. ps_cd is almost certainly the CCTNS/ICJS station namespace, making it the join key between crime records and geography. Top states: TN 2427, UP 1713, MP 1110, MH 1086, KA 1046, AP 1031, BR 929, TG 821.

name: Police station points — Survey of India / Esri LivingAtlas / MP Police
publisher: Survey of India (indiamaps.gov.in), Esri India LivingAtlas, Madhya Pradesh Police
license: CC0-1.0 per release notes, attribution requested
caveats: no ps_cd on SOI/LivingAtlas layers — cannot join to crime data directly
Esri LivingAtlas redistribution terms may conflict with the CC0 assertion
unknown vintage
evidence: Release page lists SOI_PoliceStations.geojsonl.7z, LivingAtlas_PoliceStations.geojsonl.7z and MP_Police_Stations.geojsonl.7z with per-source attribution (indiamaps.gov.in, esri.in, mppolice.gov.in) and CC0-1.0 notes. Archives not opened.
notes: Use to cross-validate MHA coordinates and to fill states where the MHA file looks thin.

name: Local Government Directory (LGD)
publisher: Ministry of Panchayati Raj
caveats: LGD codes change when units are created/merged and history is poorly versioned — maintain your own validity intervals
LGD is a CODE REGISTRY; downstream geometry comes from SOI/Bhuvan and the code-to-geometry join quality is unverified
transliteration of village names differs from Census 2011
evidence: lgdirectory.gov.in was EGRESS-BLOCKED. Existence and structure confirmed from two independent verified sources: india-geodata data/administrative/{districts,villages}/README.md name LGD_Districts and LGD_Villages release assets attributed to 'Local Government Directory, Ministry of Panchayati Raj'; ramSeraph/opendata README documents 'lgd/ - Code for pulling data from Local Government Directory (https://lgdirectory.gov.in)' with a published data mirror.
how_to_obtain: LGD exposes report/export pages rather than a documented REST API. Use the ramSeraph/opendata/lgd scraper or its mirror. Check apisetu.gov.in for a published MoPR/LGD API before writing new scraping code.
notes: Intended master geography spine for administrative units; confirmed to exist as polygon layers downstream but NOT directly verified by me.

name: Census of India 2011 administrative boundaries + Town/Village Directory
publisher: Registrar General & Census Commissioner of India
license: CC0 asserted by mirror; censusindia.gov.in terms unverified
caveats: 640 districts — 160 fewer than today's ~800
PC11 codes are a different namespace from LGD codes AND from MHA state_cd
2011 population is a 15-year-old denominator
J&K geometry predates the 2019 reorganisation into J&K and Ladakh UTs
evidence: india-geodata data/census/census-2011/README.md tabulates 8 datasets (Census_Villages, Districts_2011, SubDistricts_2011, shrug-village/subdistrict/district-pc11, PC11_TV_DIR.csv.7z), release tag census/2011, ~20 files ~1GB. data/administrative/districts/README.md confirms in-repo census-2001 and census-2011 DataMeet shapefiles. censusindia.gov.in itself EGRESS-BLOCKED.

name: Census of India 2027 (delayed decennial census)
publisher: Registrar General & Census Commissioner of India, MHA
caveats: the 2021 census never happened (COVID) so every rate until 2028 uses projected 2011 populations
projection error likely exceeds the crime variation being mapped
boundary freeze date determines which district vintage census outputs use
a NEW set of 2027 census codes will break every 2011-keyed join
evidence: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census_of_India: 2021 census 'was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic'. Houselisting 1 Apr - 30 Sep 2026 (Himalayan regions Aug-Sep 2026); population enumeration 9-28 Feb 2027; caste enumeration for the first time since 1931; digital collection with self-enumeration; basis for the next delimitation and women's reservation.
notes: Houselisting is underway as of this research date (2026-09-19).

name: Historical district boundaries 1941-2001 + district change ledger 1951-2024
publisher: India State Stories (FLAME University) / Census of India / GoI gazette notifications
caveats: polygons stop at 2001 — the 2001-2026 period, when most splits happened, is covered only by the CSV ledger, not by geometry
CSV ends 2024 and districts have been created since
LGD/PC11 codes not guaranteed present on the CSVs — verify before automating the join
evidence: data/census/historical/README.md lists 4 in-repo CSVs by exact filename (District_Timeseries_1951-2024.csv, District_splits_and_carveouts_1951_to_2024.csv, New_districts_created_1951_to_2024.csv, District_name_changes_1951_to_2021.csv), 7 decadal polygon years 1941-2001, '21 release files + 4 in-repo CSV files', and cites indiastatestory.in/datadownloads.
notes: Closest thing to an authoritative public district crosswalk. Essential for the district-reorganisation problem.

name: SHRUG — Socioeconomic High-resolution Rural-Urban Geographic Platform
publisher: Development Data Lab (Sam Asher, Paul Novosad)
caveats: CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0 — NON-COMMERCIAL ONLY; a monetised crime portal would need written permission from DDL
ShareAlike may infect derived layers
shrid is a research construct, not an administrative unit — not a display geography
get a licensing decision BEFORE shrid enters the schema
evidence: devdatalab.org EGRESS-BLOCKED. Content, the 'shrid' consistent-boundary-since-1991 definition, module list (Population Census 1991/2001/2011, Economic Census, SECC 2012, nightlights 1992-2021, forest cover, PM2.5, elections 1980-2018, PMGSY, bank branches, open polygons 2011), licence and citation all confirmed from india-geodata data/external/shrug/README.md. shrug-village-pc11/subdistrict/district assets appear under release tag census/2011.
notes: Best available tool for consistent geography over time, but the non-commercial licence is a genuine product risk.

name: Survey of India — boundary authority and map data
publisher: Survey of India, Department of Science & Technology
license: CC-BY-4.0 for index maps via DataMeet; SoI open-data terms otherwise
caveats: SoI boundaries are the ONLY legally safe depiction of J&K/Ladakh/Aksai Chin/Arunachal for a map published in India
SoI village polygons and LGD village codes are separate datasets whose join is not guaranteed 1:1
evidence: surveyofindia.gov.in EGRESS-BLOCKED. Role confirmed from en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Survey_of_India: responsible for 'scrutiny and certification of external boundaries of India and Coastline on maps published by other agencies' and for naming/spelling of geographical features; topographic maps historically sale-restricted to Indian citizens with export prohibited, liberalised 15 February 2021. Layer inventory from india-geodata data/survey-of-india/README.md (index grids 1:1M/1:250K/1:50K, outline maps, national and state boundary shapefiles) and SOI_Districts/SOI_Villages/SOI_VILLAGE_POINT release assets. indiamaps.gov.in named as the SOI police-point source.

name: Guidelines for acquiring and producing geospatial data and geospatial data services, 2021
publisher: Department of Science & Technology, Government of India
caveats: clause xiii read as quoted in a third-party README, not from the gazette PDF — counsel must verify against the original
accuracy thresholds and foreign-entity restrictions exist in this document but were NOT verified by me and must be read directly
evidence: dst.gov.in EGRESS-BLOCKED. Clause xiii reproduced verbatim in the README of github.com/ramSeraph/indian_admin_boundaries, which I fetched and read: 'For political Maps of India of any scale including national, state and other boundaries, SoI published maps or SoI digital boundary data are the standard to be used, which shall be made easily downloadable for free and their digital display and printing shall be permissible. Others may publish such maps that adhere to these standards.'
notes: The controlling legal text for our basemap's boundary depiction.

name: National Geospatial Policy 2022
publisher: Department of Science & Technology / Survey of India
caveats: PDF not opened (host blocked); cited only
evidence: URL cited in india-geodata top-level README legal notice, which I read. INDIAPOST-gov/digipin README states DIGIPIN 'Complies with the National Geospatial Policy 2022, enriching India's geospatial knowledge stack'.

name: Bhuvan national geoportal
publisher: NRSC / ISRO
caveats: bulk download is registration-gated
a separate Bhuvan_JK_Villages layer exists, implying the national village layer excludes J&K
WMS/WFS endpoint stability unverified
evidence: bhuvan.nrsc.gov.in EGRESS-BLOCKED. Layers confirmed by exact filename in india-geodata data/administrative/{districts,villages}/README.md attributed to 'Bhuvan (ISRO)': bhuvan_districts, bhuvan_villages, Bhuvan_JK_Villages. NRSC is also a DIGIPIN co-developer per the India Post README.
how_to_obtain: Free account registration for downloads; WMS/WFS services are open.

name: Bharatmaps / State GIS Portals (NICMAPS)
publisher: National Informatics Centre
caveats: JS-heavy viewers, layers frequently view-only with no export control
per-state terms of use unstated
layer naming is inconsistent across states
evidence: bharatmaps.gov.in and stategisportal.nic.in both EGRESS-BLOCKED. Platform description (NICMAPS base from SoI/ISRO/FSI/RGI at 1:50,000, ~23 layers) from an NIC Informatics PDF surfaced in search. india-geodata data/police/metadata.json names source 'State GIS Portals', url https://bharatmaps.gov.in/, authority 'Various State Police Departments' for the jurisdiction polygons.
how_to_obtain: Enumerate stategisportal.nic.in/stategisportal/Home/State/{1..38}, read each WMS GetCapabilities for a police/thana layer, pull via WFS GetFeature&outputFormat=application/json. Needs an unblocked path, ideally from India.
notes: This is the upstream the 7 states' thana polygons were harvested from — and therefore the place to find the missing 29.

name: DataMeet maps — Indian administrative and electoral boundaries
publisher: DataMeet India community
caveats: STALE — last commit 11 May 2022, so district boundaries are ~4 years out of date and miss dozens of new districts
no pincode folder at top level despite common belief
still the most-cited Indian boundary dataset, so expect other sources to be keyed to it
evidence: Fetched github.com/datameet/maps and /tree/master. Top-level folders: Country, Districts, States, Survey-of-India-Index-Maps, assembly-constituencies, divisions, docs, eci, parliamentary-constituencies, website. README states 'Unless explicitly stated, all datasets in this repository is shared under CC BY 4.0'. 475 stars, 412 forks, 81 commits, MIT on code.

name: DataMeet Municipal Spatial Data — city ward boundaries
publisher: DataMeet India community
geo_coverage: 27-28 cities: Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Bodh Gaya, Chandigarh, Chennai, Coimbatore, Delhi, Faridabad, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Kanpur, Katihar, Kishangarh, Kochi, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mira-Bhayandar, MMR, Mumbai, NMMC, PCMC, Pune, Purnia, Vadodara, Vijayawada
caveats: ward boundaries are REDRAWN at each municipal delimitation and these files carry no vintage field
a 2018 Bengaluru ward map is wrong for 2026 BBMP/GBA
coverage and layer completeness vary widely by city
MMR/NMMC/PCMC are separate bodies, not sub-areas of Mumbai/Pune
evidence: Fetched github.com/datameet/Municipal_Spatial_Data: 27 city folders (listed above), 150 stars, 186 forks, 55 commits, updated 2024-02-28, CC BY 4.0. india-geodata data/urban/municipal-boundaries/README.md tabulates 28 cities and per-city layers (ward boundaries, municipal boundary, zones/circles, facilities) in GeoJSON/KML/Shapefile. Repo README.md 404s on both main and master.
notes: Wards are the best realistic 'neighbourhood' display unit for an Indian crime map.

name: National ward and ULB boundary layers (SBM / World Bank AMRUT / Esri LivingAtlas)
publisher: Swachh Bharat Mission, World Bank AMRUT programme, Esri India
caveats: programme-administrative ward geometry may not match the corporation's legal ward map
Esri LivingAtlas redistribution terms uncertain against the CC0 claim
no vintage documented
evidence: india-geodata data/urban/wards/README.md lists 7 datasets under release tag urban/boundaries: SBM_Wards, SBM_Areas, SBM_ULBs, LivingAtlas_Wards, WB_AMRUT_Wards, WB_AMRUT_ULBs, Shillong_Wards, each in Parquet/PMTiles/GeoJSONL.7z, licensed CC0. Assets not downloaded.
notes: The route to ward coverage beyond DataMeet's 27 cities.

name: Pincode boundary polygons (DataMeet / data.gov.in / GSDL)
publisher: DataMeet community, data.gov.in, Geospatial Delhi Limited
license: CC0 for release files; DataMeet project licence for in-repo archives
caveats: pincodes are postal DELIVERY ROUTES, not areas — all polygons are reconstructions
they overlap, contain holes, and some pincodes are a single building
India Post changes them without notice
NO official pincode polygon exists, only the point directory
a pincode routinely spans multiple thanas and wards, so pincode-to-thana is many-to-many
evidence: india-geodata data/postal/README.md tabulates release tag postal/boundaries with PincodeBoundaries, Datagov_Pincode_Boundaries and GSDL_Pincodes, plus in-repo pincodes-datameet/ split shapefile archives; top-level README gives ~700 MB for the postal collection. datameet/INDIA_PINCODES seen in the org listing (33 forks, updated 2018-11-02).
notes: Valuable as a user INPUT (pincodes are what Indians know and type) but unsafe as a display or allocation unit.

name: India Post PIN code / post office directory
publisher: Department of Posts
caveats: UNVERIFIED — no URL confirmed, do not cite one until someone fetches it
evidence: indiapost.gov.in and data.gov.in both EGRESS-BLOCKED; no direct confirmation obtained. Recorded so it is not silently dropped.
how_to_obtain: Search data.gov.in for the All India Pincode Directory resource from an unblocked network.

name: DIGIPIN — India Post digital geocoded addressing system
publisher: Department of Posts, Ministry of Communications (with IIT Hyderabad and NRSC/ISRO)
caveats: DIGIPIN is a geoCODE not a geocodER — it converts coordinates to a code, it does NOT resolve a street address to coordinates, so it does not replace Nominatim
adoption is early, so few source records will carry one
4 m precision is far finer than anything we should publish — aggregate up before display
evidence: Read README.md of the official INDIAPOST-gov/digipin repo (103 stars): Apache-2.0 badge, Node.js v14+/Express v4.x, server on port 5000, Swagger at /api-docs, and two endpoints verbatim — GET /api/digipin/encode?latitude=13.11179621&longitude=80.20264269 and GET /api/digipin/decode?digipin=4P3JK852C9. 10-character alphanumeric code for a ~4m x 4m grid cell, a pure function of lat/long; built with IIT Hyderabad and NRSC (ISRO); complies with National Geospatial Policy 2022. Community fork CEPT-VZG/digipin has 414 stars.
notes: Self-hostable, no API key, no rate limit, no ToU friction. Ideal internal privacy-safe location primitive.

name: OpenStreetMap India — amenity=police POIs and administrative boundary relations
publisher: OpenStreetMap Foundation / OSM India community
caveats: ODbL share-alike: a boundary layer derived from OSM may have to be released under ODbL — keep OSM-derived geometry in a separate, separately-licensed layer
OSM admin boundaries for India are incomplete below admin_level 6 and district edits are contested
OSM's depiction of J&K/Arunachal does NOT match Survey of India and is non-compliant for publication in India
coverage figures UNVERIFIED — do not quote a police-POI count
evidence: openstreetmap.org, wiki.openstreetmap.org, taginfo.openstreetmap.org, overpass-api.de and download.geofabrik.de were all EGRESS-BLOCKED. No coverage measurement was possible.
how_to_obtain: Overpass QL: [out:json][timeout:180];area["ISO3166-1"="IN"][admin_level=2]->.in;nwr["amenity"="police"](area.in);out count; — then drop 'out count;' for features. For bulk work use the Geofabrik india-latest.osm.pbf rather than Overpass; Overpass has strict fair-use limits.

name: Nominatim (self-hosted OSM geocoder)
publisher: OpenStreetMap Foundation
caveats: Indian address quality in OSM is poor outside metros — expect low rural hit rates
no reliable house-number coverage
ODbL applies to results
the public instance caps at ~1 req/s and forbids bulk geocoding
evidence: nominatim.openstreetmap.org EGRESS-BLOCKED; recommended on architectural grounds (it is the only geocoder whose terms permit storing results and doing point-in-polygon), not from a live check.
how_to_obtain: Self-host from the Geofabrik India extract. Do not build on the public instance.

name: Photon (self-hosted OSM geocoder, typo-tolerant autocomplete)
publisher: Komoot
caveats: same ODbL and Indian-address-quality caveats as Nominatim
public instance is not for production use
evidence: photon.komoot.io EGRESS-BLOCKED. Listed as the autocomplete-friendly companion to Nominatim for the address search box.

name: Google Maps Platform (Geocoding / Places / Maps)
publisher: Google LLC
caveats: S3.2.3(c)(iv) expressly forbids using Places lat/long as input for point-in-polygon analysis — our exact operation
S3.2.3(e) No Use With Non-Google Maps forbids using Core Services with or near a non-Google map
S3.2.3(a) forbids pre-fetching, indexing, storing, resharing or rehosting geocodes
S3.2.3(b) forbids caching beyond the Service Specific Terms
Maps Service Specific Terms S1.3.2 allows caching Address Validation lat/long for only 30 consecutive calendar days
this is a blocking LEGAL constraint, not a cost constraint
evidence: Fetched cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms/ and /maps-service-terms (2.4 MB HTML), stripped markup and extracted the clauses verbatim. S3.2.3(a): 'Customer will not export, extract, or otherwise scrape Google Maps Content for use outside the Services... (ii) bulk download Google Maps tiles, Street View images, geocodes, directions...'. S3.2.3(c): '...(iv) use latitude/longitude values from the Places API as an input for point-in-polygon analysis'. S3.2.3(e): 'Customer will not use the Google Maps Core Services with or near a non-Google Map in a Customer Application'. S1.3.2: '30 consecutive calendar days, after which Customer must delete the cached Google Maps Content'.
notes: DO NOT USE. Recorded so the decision is documented and not revisited.

name: Mapbox (geocoding and vector tiles)
publisher: Mapbox Inc.
caveats: standard geocoding forbids permanent storage; permanent geocoding is a separate, costlier SKU that must be matched to our store-and-serve model
boundary depiction for J&K/Arunachal must be checked against Survey of India requirements
NO terms verified by me
evidence: mapbox.com and docs.mapbox.com both EGRESS-BLOCKED. Recorded for Phase 2 legal review, not for reliance.

name: HERE Location Services
publisher: HERE Global B.V.
caveats: generally more permissive on result storage than Google but requires contract review
Indian address coverage quality unknown
NO terms verified by me
evidence: here.com EGRESS-BLOCKED. Recorded for completeness.

name: Mappls / MapmyIndia (CE Info Systems)
publisher: CE Info Systems Ltd
caveats: commercial licensing and per-call pricing unverified
NO terms verified by me
evidence: mapmyindia.com, about.mappls.com and www.mappls.com all EGRESS-BLOCKED; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mappls and /wiki/CE_Info_Systems both returned 404. No information verified.
notes: Strongest commercial candidate on paper: Indian-origin, ISRO/government tie-in, and the one vendor whose India boundary depiction is compliant by construction — exactly where OSM is weakest. Needs a real evaluation in Phase 2.

name: indianopenmaps — tile server for ~498 Indian geospatial layers
publisher: ramSeraph (community)
caveats: per-layer licences vary and are not centrally stated
community-run infrastructure with no SLA — mirror anything we depend on
evidence: Read the repo README: Hono-based Cloudflare Worker serving vector (protobuf) and raster tiles from PMTiles archives and COGs, mosaic mode for sharded PMTiles, TileJSON per source, a STAC API over geoparquet indices with flatbush spatial indexing, MapLibre GL viewers with feature inspection; 'Currently serves ~498 tile sources'. Ships iomaps, a Python CLI that clips the large .7z archives to a polygon/bbox and exports to other formats. Backed by 11 data repos including indian_admin_boundaries and indian_facilities.
notes: Proves the PMTiles + MapLibre architecture works at scale for Indian data; iomaps solves 'I only want Bengaluru'.

name: ramSeraph/indian_admin_boundaries — harvested GoI boundary layers
publisher: ramSeraph (community harvest of Government of India portals)
license: varies per layer; README reproduces Geospatial Guidelines clause xiii as the governing constraint
caveats: community harvest, not an official redistribution channel
per-layer vintage undocumented
upstream portals may change or withdraw layers without notice
evidence: Read the repo README: release tags states, districts, subdistricts, blocks, panchayats, villages, habitations, urban, forests, coastal, postal, police, constituencies, census-2011, historical. README quotes Geospatial Guidelines clause xiii verbatim as the usability test for boundary data. Police release page independently verified (13 assets).
notes: The true upstream of india-geodata's boundary content — prefer citing this over the mirror.

name: ramSeraph/opendata — LGD and Survey of India scrapers + data mirror
publisher: ramSeraph (community)
caveats: mirror freshness depends on when the maintainer last ran the scraper
no licence stated on the mirrored data
github.io mirror was EGRESS-BLOCKED to me, so the data itself is unverified
evidence: Read the repo README: 'lgd/ - Code for pulling data from Local Government Directory (https://lgdirectory.gov.in) - data at ramseraph.github.io/opendata/lgd'; 'maps/SOI/ - Code for pulling data from Survey Of India (https://onlinemaps.surveyofindia.gov.in)'. Repo topics include LGD, SOI, maps, opendata. Last updated 2026-04-03.
notes: The practical way to obtain LGD in bulk without writing a new scraper against a JS portal.

name: datta07/INDIAN-SHAPEFILES
publisher: datta07 (community)
caveats: 2019 vintage: README warns 'Some datasets reflect 2019 administrative boundaries. Recent territorial changes may not be reflected in all files'
no police layer is documented in its README despite india-geodata citing it for police points — trust the file, not the attribution chain
village boundaries are on the roadmap but absent
evidence: Fetched the repo README: national level (India, states, districts, PCs, national highways, railways), state level (state->district->sub-district plus constituencies), metropolitan level (ward and sub-division boundaries). GeoJSON RFC 7946 + shapefile, EPSG:4326, UTF-8, MIT licence, vintage 'Primarily 2019 (with ongoing updates)'.

name: Police Jurisdiction Maps for Major Cities of India (OpenCity CKAN)
publisher: OpenCity / Oorvani Foundation
caveats: dataset contents, city list and formats all unverified
may be image maps rather than vector data
evidence: Dataset title and URL surfaced in search results; both data.opencity.in and opencity.in were EGRESS-BLOCKED. A search snippet indicated a Mumbai police jurisdictions map with station locations.
how_to_obtain: Open the CKAN dataset page from an unblocked network; CKAN exposes /api/3/action/package_show for machine access.
notes: Worth chasing specifically for Mumbai/Maharashtra, which is absent from every polygon source found.

name: Geospatial Delhi Limited (GSDL) GIS layers
publisher: Geospatial Delhi Limited, Government of NCT of Delhi
caveats: GSDL's own portal terms unverified
vintage unknown
evidence: GSDL named as the source of GSDL_DL_Police_Station_Boundaries and GSDL_Pincodes in two verified sources (the indian_admin_boundaries police release page and india-geodata data/postal/README.md). The datameet Google Group thread 'Shape files for Police Jurisdiction Maps of Delhi' was EGRESS-BLOCKED.
notes: Delhi is the single best-served city: thana polygons, pincode polygons and ward data all available.

name: Compliant basemap architecture: MapLibre + PMTiles + Survey of India boundary overlay
publisher: n/a (recommended architecture, not a third-party source)
license: mixed: ODbL for OSM-derived cartography, Survey of India terms for boundaries
caveats: if the cartographic basemap is OSM-derived, its own boundary lines must be SUPPRESSED and replaced by the SoI layer, not merely overdrawn — an OSM dashed LoC still visible beneath our line remains a non-compliant depiction
counsel must sign off against Geospatial Guidelines clause xiii before public launch
evidence: Architecture derived from the verified clause xiii text (SoI maps or SoI digital boundary data are the standard for political maps of India) and the verified indianopenmaps README demonstrating PMTiles + MapLibre at ~498 layers. Not itself a fetched product.
notes: The only configuration that is simultaneously legally compliant in India, free of Google ToS conflicts, and capable of the vector styling a crime map needs. Publication cadence not stated by the publisher.
